description: Required. The Participant this Demography record belongs to. Production builds it as uuid5(https://w3id.org/bdchm/Participant, <subject id> + :<COHORT>).

Optional. The Visit (exam, form or record) whose table supplied the value. Production writes one Demography block per source table that carries sex, race or ethnicity, each linked to that table's visit, so one participant can have several Demography records. Leave empty for cohort-level tables with no visit.

Biological sex (SexEnum: MALE, FEMALE, UNKNOWN). Older cohorts label this 'gender'; when the values are male/female it maps here. Single-sex cohorts set a constant (production: WHI writes FEMALE for every participant). Where sex is only implied by a skip instruction (FHS 'Male Participant (if male skip ...)' checkbox), production maps checked to MALE and everything else to FEMALE; use this only when the item was asked of every participant. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.
A person who belongs to the sex that normally produces sperm. Meaning OMOP:8507. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.
A person who belongs to the sex that normally produces ova. Meaning OMOP:8532. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.

Not known, not observed, not recorded, or refused. Meaning OMOP:45877986. Use for an explicit source code such as 'Unknown or other' (production: LTRC GENDER 'UNK'). Leave the slot empty when the value is simply missing. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.

Race (RaceEnum, multivalued). Rules: (1) A Hispanic/Latino code inside a race or combined race/ethnicity variable sets ethnicity HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; production then writes race UNKNOWN for that code (MESA race1c=4, WHI RACE=4). (2) 'Other' or 'Some other race' has no BDC-HM value; production maps it to UNKNOWN. (3) More than one race: production writes the single value MORE_THAN_ONE_RACE when two or more race boxes are checked (FHS, WHI) or the source says multiracial; BDC-HM also allows listing each race, which is open (see questions). (4) Historical labels: 'Negro' and 'Colored' are BLACK_OR_AFRICAN_AMERICAN (the BDC-HM definition names 'Negro'); 'Caucasian' is WHITE; 'Chinese American', 'Oriental' and Asian subgroups (Asian Indian, Chinese, Filipino, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese) are ASIAN; Native Hawaiian, Guamanian or Chamorro, Samoan are NATIVE_HAWAIIAN_OR_OTHER_PACIFIC_ISLANDER. (5) A combined 'Asian/Pacific Islander' code cannot be split; production maps it to ASIAN. (6) 'Indian' alone is ambiguous (American Indian vs Asian Indian): check the codebook. (7) Single-race cohorts set a constant (production: JHS writes BLACK_OR_AFRICAN_AMERICAN). (8) A variable that records only one comparison (ARIC PULM21 RACE 'Whites'/'Otherwise') maps only the named category; leave the rest empty. (9) When no race box is checked (sum 0 or all null) leave race empty; use MORE_THAN_ONE_RACE only for 2 or more checked boxes. (10) FHS race_sum 88 'Defaulted race (White)' is mapped to WHITE; an issue is to be raised with the cohort. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.

description: A person having more than one race. Meaning OMOP:45880900. Use for a 'More than one race', 'Multi-race' or 'Mixed' code, or (production rule) when two or more race boxes are checked. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.

Not known, not observed, not recorded, or refused. Meaning OMOP:45877986. Use for explicit unknown, refused, 'prefer not to answer' and (production) 'Other' codes, and for the Hispanic code of a combined race/ethnicity variable. Leave the slot empty when the value is simply missing. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.
Example source variable description: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BEST DESCRIBES YOU? (CHECK ALL THAT APPLY): PREFER NOT TO ANSWER

description: Hispanic or Latino origin (EthnicityEnum). Rules: (1) Any Hispanic subgroup answered yes (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Dominican, other Hispanic) is HISPANIC_OR_LATINO. (2) A combined race/ethnicity variable: its Hispanic code is HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; codes worded 'not Hispanic' (e.g. 'White (not of Hispanic origin)', 'Black, not Hispanic') are NOT_HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; plain race codes ('WHITE') say nothing about ethnicity, leave empty. (3) Paired checkboxes (Hispanic / Not Hispanic) map each box. (4) A cohort recruited as entirely Hispanic/Latino sets a constant (production: HCHS/SOL writes HISPANIC_OR_LATINO). (5) FHS eth_sum 88 'Defaulted ethnicity (Not Hispanic or Latino)' is mapped to NOT_HISPANIC_OR_LATINO; an issue is to be raised with the cohort. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.

A person of Cuban, Mexican, Puerto Rican, South or Central American, or other Spanish culture or origin, regardless of race (OMB). Meaning OMOP:38003563. The transform spec may hold the enum name or its meaning CURIE; the ingest pipeline emits the CURIE.
Example source variable description: Are you Spanish/Hispanic/Latino|WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BEST DESCRIBES YOU? (CHECK ALL THAT APPLY): SPANISH/HISPANIC/LATINO|MEXICAN, CHICANO, MEXICAN-AMERICAN|WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BEST DESCRIBES YOU - ETHNICITY HISPANIC OR LATINO
